name: Brick Studio
description: A 3D toy-brick build a Charm makes from chat: place parts on a stud grid, check what holds, and look at the result. The build is LDraw text in the document

charmiq.command.name: listParts
charmiq.command.description: The grid conventions, every catalog part's name by kind, the colors and a figure's faces. Call first; findParts gives the rows of the parts you will use

parts.description: One line per kind: the kind, then its part names

frameFaces.description: The faces a figure wears on a stage's frame alone (a film's, never a build's): each a two-sided head's back

charmiq.command.name: findParts
charmiq.command.description: The rows (name, width x depth x height, which way it descends, fills) of the catalog parts a query names, best first. A query is part names, a size such as 2x4, a kind, or a word such as roof, tree, animal or car

query.description: e.g. brick-2x4 slope-45-2x2, or roof, or 2x4

limit.description: The most rows to return (12 when omitted)

total.description: Parts the query names, all of them

charmiq.command.name: listPlacedParts
charmiq.command.description: The parts and copies of components in a set of the build with their positions, a page at a time: pass next back as from for the next page

from.description: The index to start at (the previous page's next)

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

parts.description: Each with its step when the build has more than one, and pinned: true when it is pinned; a line placing a component that is not a copy on the grid is listed by component, color and at (a cell it fills: removeParts there removes the line)

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

next.description: Set while parts remain: the next page's from

unchecked.description: Parts off the grid or outside the catalog

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: addParts
charmiq.command.description: Place parts and copies of components. A batch that would collide is refused whole. Returns the check of the build it made: no check call is needed after. pinned: true holds a part where it stands though nothing holds it up (a brick flying from an explosion, a fake ceiling a chandelier hangs from)

items.description: A part (part, color) or a copy of a component (component)

component.description: A component's name, to place a copy of it instead of a part

pinned.description: Held where it stands, though nothing holds it up: what the design means to float (a brick flying from an explosion, a fake ceiling a chandelier hangs from, a false wall). A copy is pinned whole

pose.description: A figure's pose, each limb in degrees (a multiple of 15; a limb left out is 0). An arm or leg swings forward: 90 points it ahead, 180 straight up, -30 back; the head turns clockwise seen from above. A figure's level is its lowest point: seated (legs at 90) on a seat, that is the seat's top

legColor.description: A figure's hips and legs color (catalog color; blue when left out)

skin.description: A figure's head and hands color (catalog color; yellow when left out): light-gray for a black-and-white film

face.description: A figure's face: smile (the default), grin, laugh, lopsided, surprised, scowl, frown, moustache, sunglasses, freckles, beard or glasses (listParts names them)

hat.description: What a figure wears on its head (listParts names them): part and color

rightHand.description: What a figure holds in its right hand (listParts names them): part, color and, to hold it another way than its first, grip

leftHand.description: What a figure holds in its left hand (listParts names them): part, color and, to hold it another way than its first, grip

angle.description: A hinge's angle, degrees (0 when left out): hinge-1x2 tilts its top (90 raises its south side upright), the others swivel it clockwise seen from above

carry.description: The copy of a component a hinge carries, where it stands with the hinge at 0: on the hinge's top (its level the level of the hinge's studs, its footprint over at least one of them). It turns with the top

sides.description: The copies of components a part with side faces carries, by face (north, east, south, west, as at rotation 0; listParts names each part's faces): each where it stands on the face's map, seen from outside (x right, z up, x 0 z 0 its first stud), covering at least one stud

newStep.description: Put these parts in a new building step after the last

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one
The set acted on, when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: defineComponent
charmiq.command.description: Define a component: a group of parts in its own grid (x, z and level from 0), placed many times with addParts. Its hinges and side faces carry other components (carry, sides) that carry none themselves: a store's sign band carrying its signs. Defining a name again replaces it and changes every copy; refused whole if a copy would then collide, or if a component carried would come to carry. Returns its size and the build's check

name.description: Lower case letters, digits and dashes, e.g. tower

pose.description: A figure's pose, as addParts takes it

legColor.description: A figure's hips and legs color, as addParts takes it

skin.description: A figure's head and hands color, as addParts takes it

face.description: A figure's face, as addParts takes it (the smile when left out)

hat.description: What a figure wears on its head, as addParts takes it

rightHand.description: What a figure holds in its right hand, as addParts takes it

leftHand.description: What a figure holds in its left hand, as addParts takes it

angle.description: A hinge's angle, as addParts takes it

carry.description: The copy of a component a hinge carries, as addParts takes it: a component that carries none itself (a component nests one deep)

sides.description: The copies of components a part's side faces carry, as addParts takes them: each a component that carries none itself (a component nests one deep)

size.description: width x depth x height at rotation 0 (studs, studs, levels)

set.description: The set the check covers (the set shown), when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: defineComponentFromDesign
charmiq.command.description: Define a component from a saved design, by its uri from listDesigns (or its name), its footprint from x 0, z 0 and its lowest part at level 0; place copies with addParts. Its ground and steps are left out, and its parts off the grid are counted in leftOut. Named after the design unless name is given; a component of that name is redefined, every copy with it

design.description: The saved design's name, when no uri is given

name.description: The component's name (lower case letters, digits and dashes); the design's own name made one when omitted

size.description: width x depth x height at rotation 0 (studs, studs, levels)

leftOut.description: Parts of the design off the grid, left out

otherSets.description: The design's sets past its first, left out: a component is made from the first

set.description: The set the check covers (the set shown), when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: listComponents
charmiq.command.description: The components the build defines, which every set may place: name, size (width x depth x height at rotation 0, its own parts: what its hinges and faces carry may reach past it), parts (what its hinges and faces carry included) and copies placed (and copiesBySet, by set, when the build has more than one). With component, that component's own parts instead, each where it stands in the component as a copy of it holds them (a part in LDraw's inherited color, which takes each copy's, listed as inherited; with no copy, its parts as defined), a page at a time (pass next back as from): the address a stage's placed actor names a part inside a copy by (placed.inside)

component.description: A component's name: list its own parts

from.description: The index to start at (the previous page's next)

parts.description: With component: each of its parts as addParts places one, where it stands in the component

next.description: Set while parts remain: the next page's from

charmiq.command.name: listSets
charmiq.command.description: The build's sets, the first first: each an arrangement on its own baseplate (a film's street, its garage) sharing the build's components, with its parts, copies, steps, ground and sky; and the set the studio shows. A build of more than one set takes set on every command that reads or edits one

smoothGround.description: true when its ground is smooth (setGround)

sky.description: Its sky, when it has one (setSky)

charmiq.command.name: addSet
charmiq.command.description: Add a set to the build and show it: empty, or a copy of the set from names (its parts, copies, steps and ground: the street at night). A build holds at most 32 sets

name.description: The set's name: 1 to 40 characters, no other set's (ignoring case)

from.description: The set to copy, by name

charmiq.command.name: renameSet
charmiq.command.description: Rename a set (the first, Main until it is named, included)

set.description: The set, by name (when the build has one, it may be left out)

name.description: Its new name: 1 to 40 characters, no other set's (ignoring case)

charmiq.command.name: removeSet
charmiq.command.description: Remove a set and everything in it (never the build's last set; clear empties that). The first set removed, the next becomes the first

set.description: The set, by name

charmiq.command.name: removeParts
charmiq.command.description: Remove the part that fills each given cell (a cell of a copy, or of any line placing a component, removes that whole line). Returns the check of the build it made (no check call is needed after) and the parts the removal left unsupported

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one
The set acted on, when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: pinParts
charmiq.command.description: Pin the part that fills each given cell where it stands, though nothing holds it up: what the design means to float (a brick flying from an explosion, a fake ceiling a chandelier hangs from, a false wall); a cell of a copy pins the whole copy. A pinned part is held and holds what stands on it or hangs from it, and still collides. pinned: false unpins. Hold what should stand the real way (a floor laid into its wall's courses); never pin to quiet the check. Returns the check of the build it made

pinned.description: true (when left out) pins, false unpins

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

pinnedParts.description: The parts pinned (one pinned already is left out)

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: setGround
charmiq.command.description: Color a set's baseplate (grass, a road, sand) instead of covering it with plates. Any catalog color that is not see-through; omit the color for the theme's. smooth: true draws it without studs (a road, a tabletop); parts still stand on it at level 0

smooth.description: true for a ground without studs (a road, a tabletop); it names its color

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

smooth.description: true when the ground is smooth

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: addPicture
charmiq.command.description: Stand a picture from the Drive in a set (a billboard, a poster, a painted backdrop, or flat as a rug), or several in one write: picture a list, refused whole when one is. Its panel collides with a part it stands inside, and with a picture in its plane where they cross (two panels in one stud row, or flat on one level, flicker over each other); refused, and the check names it: hang an upright one in a free stud row, such as the row before a wall's face, beside or above the pictures there (or in the row before one, to stand in front), or stand it on a top; lay a flat one on a top, where parts may stand on it. Its width and height are studs where its level is plates (2.5 plates a stud): the answer names the level its top reaches

picture.description: The picture (an image from the Drive placed as a part is), or a list of pictures written in one write

image.description: A picture from the Drive (charmiq://file/...), or one Brick Studio ships, by name (listPictures names them)

x.description: The south-west corner of its footprint, studs east

z.description: The south-west corner of its footprint, studs north

level.description: Its bottom, in plates above the baseplate

rotation.description: Clockwise seen from above; upright at 0 it faces south

height.description: Studs, as width is (2.5 plates a stud: 16 studs high rises 40 levels); the image's own shape when left out

flat.description: Lying on its level, its top edge north at rotation 0, rather than standing

fit.description: cover fills it, cropping the overflow (the default); contain shows the image whole; stretch fills it with the whole image

image.description: A picture from the Drive (charmiq://file/...), or one Brick Studio ships, by name (listPictures names them)

x.description: The south-west corner of its footprint, studs east

z.description: The south-west corner of its footprint, studs north

level.description: Its bottom, in plates above the baseplate

rotation.description: Clockwise seen from above; upright at 0 it faces south

height.description: Studs, as width is (2.5 plates a stud: 16 studs high rises 40 levels); the image's own shape when left out

flat.description: Lying on its level, its top edge north at rotation 0, rather than standing

fit.description: cover fills it, cropping the overflow (the default); contain shows the image whole; stretch fills it with the whole image

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

picture.description: The picture as written, or each in the order given

index.description: Its place among the set's pictures (removePicture takes it), or each one's

top.description: The level an upright picture's top reaches (plates), or each one's (null for a flat one, or one taking its image's shape); absent when none has one

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: listPictures
charmiq.command.description: The pictures standing in a set, in order: each as addPicture takes it, its place in the list the index removePicture takes; and the pictures Brick Studio ships, by name

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

shipped.description: The pictures Brick Studio ships, by the name image takes

set.description: The set read, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: removePicture
charmiq.command.description: Remove a picture from a set by its place among the set's pictures (listPictures lists them, 0 the first), or several in one write: index a list of places, each named once (clear takes a set's every picture with its parts)

index.description: The picture's place, or a list of places

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

removed.description: The picture removed, or each removed in the order named

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: setSky
charmiq.command.description: Put a sky behind a set: generated from a horizon and a zenith color with seeded clouds, or a picture from the Drive (a panorama wraps the whole sky; any other picture is tiled round the horizon). lights lets it light the set too. Omit the sky for the theme's backdrop

sky.description: The sky; omit it for the theme's backdrop

seed.description: Which clouds: another seed draws others alike

image.description: A picture from the Drive (charmiq://file/...), or one Brick Studio ships, by name, in place of the generated sky

lights.description: The sky lights the set as well as standing behind it

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one

sky.description: The sky as written, or theme

set.description: The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: clear
charmiq.command.description: Remove every part, copy, picture, set but the first and component, and any file the build carries (a film's scene), keeping the first set's name, ground and sky. With set, empty that set alone, its pictures too (its name, ground and sky kept, the components every set shares left). With expect, only while the build is still that text

expect.description: The build's text as last read (getModel): refused, nothing changed, once the build is no longer that text

set.description: The one set to empty, by name (listSets names them)
The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: check
charmiq.command.description: Find collisions and parts not held up from a set's baseplate, for a build that changed other than by addParts or removeParts (whose results carry it). Never ok while the build was read only in part or the document holds more than one build

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one
The set acted on, when the build has more than one

pinned.description: Parts pinned where they stand (held, though nothing holds them up)

strayPins.description: Pins naming a cell no part fills

truncated.description: Set when the build expands past what Brick Studio reads: only part of it was read

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: setView
charmiq.command.description: Turn the camera, framing the build unless fit is false. Use before a screenshot

azimuth.description: Degrees: 0 looks north from the south, 90 west from the east

charmiq.command.name: lookAround
charmiq.command.description: Show a set of the build from all four sides at once (south, east, north, west, each framed) so one screenshot sees every side. Take that screenshot after each object and at the end. The next change closes it

set.description: The set to act on, by name (listSets names them): needed when the build has more than one
The set acted on, when the build has more than one

charmiq.command.name: probeStage
charmiq.command.description: What stands where on a stage of these sets and actors (staged or not; the pieces cast left out, nothing shown): the part filling each point, and the first part each segment crosses from its start (glass, a trans- color, window and door frames and fences hide nothing; the part holding a segment's end does not count; a part a hinge or face carries is judged by itself and named by its carrier). Points are the film's: x and z in studs within 400 of the origin, height in plates within 2000 of the baseplate; at most 20000 points, segments and grounds a call; the ground under a footprint answered as every surface an actor there could stand on. Only parts on the grid fill cells, as collisions count them. A film's camera is checked with it: inside a part, or a part between it and its target. Asked held, it answers where each figure's hand holds a hand item: the position and turn a frame gives an actor cast as that item to stand exactly there, so a film stands a thing a hand lets go of where the hand held it and reads which way it points (from its grip to its far end)

ldraw.description: LDraw text standing for the build, as stage takes it (leave it out for the build)

sets.description: The sets of the stage, as stage takes them

actors.description: The stage's actors, as stage takes them: the pieces cast are left out of their set

set.description: The set probed, one of sets (the first when left out)

grounds.description: Footprints to read the ground under: each its middle and size in studs (at most 64 each way), turned by its yaw

shot.description: A figure's shot, as frame takes it

item.description: A hand item { part, color, grip? }, as addParts dresses a hand

held.description: Hands to answer where they hold a hand item

points.description: Each point's part, named, or null

segments.description: Each segment's first part, named, or null

grounds.description: The surfaces under each footprint in plates, lowest first: each top of a part's cells nothing stands on (seen through or not), and 0 where the baseplate is bare under it

studded.description: Beside grounds, whether each surface is studded under the footprint: the baseplate's studs, or a part's top studs at that level, in every column under it holding the surface (a tile's top is smooth)

tops.description: Beside grounds, the part whose top each surface is, by its kind and color (tile-2x4 orange; a part a hinge or face carries by itself): the one holding it under most of the footprint, the first found of as many; null for the baseplate

extent.description: The area the set's parts stand over, whole studs: its south-west corner and size; absent for a set without parts

held.description: Beside held, where each hand holds its item: the position and turn a frame gives an actor cast as that item to stand exactly there, and where the hand's grip on it (grip: its bar's point at the grip's centre) and its far end stand (tip: the end of that bar farthest from the hand, a spear's point), the way it points from the hand, and its near end (butt: the bar's other end, behind the hand)

charmiq.command.name: describeStage
charmiq.command.description: Whether a film scene is staged in place of the build (stage), whether the person went back to the build since, whether the studio holds a build of its own, its build's sets, the reel staged (its number, as show and loadReel name it, and its header) while the stage holds one, and the actor it follows through the film (follow), while it follows one. Asked figures, every figure built as a part of a copy of a component in the first set, at the placed address that casts it (a stand's seated audience)

figures.description: List the figures built as parts of the first set's copies

sets.description: The build's sets by name, the first first

reel.description: The reel staged, while the stage holds one: its number and its header as stage took it

followed.description: The actor followed through the film, its ghosts and path drawn

figures.description: Asked figures, each figure built as a part of a copy, copy by copy: its component, where the copy stands and where the figure stands inside it (placed { ...copy, inside } casts it) and where it rests there, as stage's placed answers it

charmiq.command.name: stage
charmiq.command.description: Show a scene in place of the build: its sets (the build's, or those of the LDraw text given; one stands at a time, a frame naming which) and actors, each a component, a dressed catalog part, or a piece standing in a set by where it stands (placed: its set is then shown without it, and placed in the answer says where it stands), that frame then puts anywhere; an actor is drawn in whichever set stands. Nothing is written to the build; unstage shows it again. Use it for a still (the car in mid-air) or a film's frames

ldraw.description: LDraw text standing for the build, its components the actors' (the build when left out)

sets.description: The sets the stage stands, by name, the first standing first and a frame's set showing in its place (the first set alone when left out)

actors.description: Each actor once, by name: { name, component }, { name, part, color, legColor?, skin?, hat?, rightHand?, leftHand? } dressed as addParts dresses a figure, a hand item { name, part, color, grip? } standing alone (its position its box's bottom middle), or { name, placed: { x, z, level } }, the part or copy standing there in the set as listPlacedParts gives it, or with placed.inside one part of that copy, cast alone (a clerk in a store's copy, the copy shown without it); a part is cast once, whole or within its copy

placed.description: Where the piece stands in its set: { set?, x, z, level, inside? }, as listPlacedParts gives it (in the first set staged when set is left out); inside { x, z, level } names the part of the copy standing there by where it stands in its component, as listComponents with component lists them

skin.description: A figure's head and hands color, as addParts takes it

face.description: A figure's face, as addParts takes it

grip.description: A hand item's grip, as addParts takes it: where a hand holds it

floor.description: The area (studs) the baseplate covers at least, so actors have ground to move over: { x, z, width, depth }, its south-west corner and size

light.description: How the stage is lit over the look's own light: { key, fill, exposure, soft, white, saturation, from }, the key light scaled (0 to 3), the fill (the studio's environment and sky) scaled (0 to 4), the exposure scaled (0.25 to 4) and the key's shadows softened (0 the look's own to 1 the softest); each 1 (soft 0) when left out. white: a white balance, a color temperature 1700 to 25000 kelvin (6500 neutral, lower warmer) or tungsten, warm, neutral, cool or shade. saturation: 0 (gray) to 2 (1 the look's own). from: where the key light stands, { azimuth, elevation } as setView names a direction (azimuth 0 south of the set, 90 east; elevation 1 to 90)

sky.description: The stage's sky over every set's own (a film's sky): { horizon, zenith, clouds, seed } or { image }, with lights, as setSky takes it; each set's own when left out

reel.description: A film, for Applications: its frames a second (at most 60), length in frames (at most 7200) and the size its frames are drawn at. loadReel then loads its frames

fps.description: Frames a second: a whole number, or a film rate (24000 / 1001)

view.description: The view of the reel's frames this studio shows (the main camera when left out)

marks.description: What a plan view draws over the set, for Applications: paths along the ground, each { label, color: #rrggbb, dashed (where it stands for something hidden), points: [{ x, z }] } (at most 256 paths, 7200 points each, 50000 in all)

keep.description: For Applications staging a film again: the picture standing (its actors where they stood) stays until a frame shows, never the set bare between. A first stage, or one with keep left out, shows the first set alone until a frame shows its actors

wheeled.description: The actors with wheels, which frame's rolled turns

figures.description: The actors that pose (figures), which frame's pose turns

bottoms.description: What a figure's lowest point is measured from: its core's box and each limb's at each 15-degree angle, each its bottom and top over its soles (plates) and its reach across (x) and along (z) its footprint's middle (studs, least first). A figure's height is its lowest point; standing, its soles stand its pose's rise below it, and turned, its hips stand over it by as far as its turned boxes' deepest corner lies under them

clicks.description: The actors that click onto studs (figures and creatures): on studs they stand on them, a stud at a time

sizes.description: Each actor's box, unturned and unposed: studs across (x), studs along (z), plates up; a figure's as it measures, hands included (3.12 by 1.85 studs), never the whole cells it reaches into

grips.description: Where a hand holds each hand item actor: its grip's centre from its position in its own frame (studs east, plates up, studs north)

placed.description: Each placed actor's rest: the position and turn a frame gives it to stand where its piece stood (a posed figure's position is its unposed frame's: a seated one's 2 plates below its seat), and a posed figure's pose there (a frame's pose names only the limbs it turns: what a film adds moves from this)

reel.description: The reel's number, when one is staged

charmiq.command.name: loadReel
charmiq.command.description: Load a page of the staged reel's frames, for Applications: at most 240 frames from the count loaded so far, each { set?, actors, camera, views?, transition?, fade?, fadeColor?, fadeShape?, title? } (set, actors and camera as frame takes them, views by name, each a camera or a plan { plan: { x, z, width, depth } } looking straight down over that area; transition { camera, set?, actors?, left, shape }: the shot the frame leaves, through its camera on its set (with its actors as they stood when on another set), how much of it still shows from 1 to 0, and dissolve, wipe-left, wipe-right, wipe-up, wipe-down or iris; fade from 0 to 1, to fadeColor #rrggbb (black when left out), over the whole picture or closing as fadeShape iris; title { text, style: card or caption, opacity? }). A page with a frame that is not one is refused whole

charmiq.command.name: show
charmiq.command.description: Show a loaded frame of the staged reel, for Applications. Without capture it answers at once and the newest frame asked is shown next; with capture it answers that exact frame as an image, its fade and title drawn

playing.description: Whether the film plays, for the studio's controls full screen (a live frame alone)

image.description: The frame captured (an ImageBitmap), when capture was given

charmiq.command.name: follow
charmiq.command.description: Follow an actor through the staged reel, for Applications: at each frame shown live, the actor's ghosts at each drawing within before and after seconds (red behind, green ahead, fainter further off) and its path through its hips with its keys marked, never in a capture or a thumbnail. Without an actor, follow no one. Staging again follows no one

actor.description: The cast actor to follow; leave it out to follow no one

before.description: Seconds of ghosts behind the frame shown, 0 to 10 (2)

after.description: Seconds of ghosts ahead of the frame shown, 0 to 10 (2)

keys.description: The film's seconds of the actor's keys, marked on its path

charmiq.command.name: thumbnail
charmiq.command.description: A loaded frame of the staged reel as a small picture (at most 480 a side), for Applications, through one of the frame's views when named; the frame shown stays as it is

view.description: One of the frame's views (this studio's own camera when left out)

charmiq.command.name: storyboard
charmiq.command.description: Show a storyboard of the staged reel, for Applications: up to 12 loaded frames on a sheet over the stage, each { frame, caption }, drawn through one of the frames' views when named. Resolves once the sheet shows, so an Application screenshot next reads them all; the next frame shown or staged closes it

shown.description: The frames shown; none when the sheet was closed first

charmiq.command.name: frame
charmiq.command.description: Show one moment of the staged scene: each actor where its shot puts it (any others hidden), through a camera. An actor's position is the middle of the bottom of its footprint, turned about that point; a figure's x and z are its hips, its height its lowest point as it is turned (a seated figure's seat, as a build places it; lying on its back, its head's back), and it turns about its hips; yaw turns it clockwise seen from above, pitch raises its south side (a figure's front), roll its west side; a figure's pose takes any angle; rolled turns its wheels as the actor having rolled that many studs along its own north. capture answers the frame as an image, for Applications

set.description: The staged set the moment stands on (the first staged when left out)

position.description: Where the middle of the bottom of its footprint stands (a figure's hips across the ground, its lowest point up)

pose.description: A figure's limbs in degrees: head, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg; and joints a frame alone turns: lean (its torso and hips forward together over its legs, which keep their place), rightWrist and leftWrist (each hand on its forearm, the left mirroring the right); and twist, no joint (a toy figure has no waist): the whole figure turned from its feet, clockwise seen from above, added to its turn's yaw

face.description: A figure's face in this frame alone (its own when left out), as addParts takes it

rightHand.description: What a figure's right hand holds in this frame alone, { part, color, grip? } as addParts takes it, or null for nothing (what it holds as dressed when left out)

leftHand.description: What a figure's left hand holds in this frame alone, as rightHand

rolled.description: Studs the actor has rolled along its own north: each wheel set turns by its share (backward when turned round, not at all when turned across)

target.description: The point it looks at and focuses on

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (32 when left out)

roll.description: Degrees the camera turns clockwise about where it looks, as seen from behind it (level when left out)

shift.description: The lens shifted up by this share of the picture's height, down when negative, its verticals kept upright: a level camera at -0.37 looks down at the floor below its horizon, which stands 0.13 down the picture. Blender's vertical lens shift against the picture's height (Blender's shift_y is against its larger side). Unshifted when left out

focus.description: What is sharp: a point { x, z, height }, or a number of studs ahead along the view (the target when left out)

aperture.description: The lens's opening as an f-number, a real lens at a brick's scale: a long lens (a narrow fov) or a near focus blurs more. Through 32 degrees focused 20 studs ahead, 2 leaves only what it focuses on sharp, 8 is a macro's, 22 a toy photo's, 64 nearly all sharp. Given, the frame has a depth of field at every look; left out, the look's own (Photo's f/22, none below)

capture.description: For Applications: the frame's size in pixels, { width, height }; the answer carries it as an image

image.description: The captured frame (an ImageBitmap), when capture was given

charmiq.command.name: unstage
charmiq.command.description: Show the build again in place of the staged scene

charmiq.command.name: setFidelity
charmiq.command.description: Set how real the bricks look: 0 Draft, 1 Plastic, 2 Shaded, 3 Photo, 4 Path traced (slow; falls back to 3 where unavailable; past 3,000 parts shown it draws as Photo, and untraced says why). Resolves once settled, so a screenshot next shows it

charmiq.command.name: getModel
charmiq.command.description: The build as LDraw text, a page of whole lines at a time: pass nextLine back as fromLine for the next page. While the document holds more than one build: the conflict and each build's LDraw text, to recover from

fromLine.description: The line to start at (the previous page's nextLine)

nextLine.description: Set while lines remain: the next page's fromLine

conflict.description: Set when the document holds more than one build: why, and how to recover. Edits are refused until one remains

charmiq.command.name: setModel
charmiq.command.description: Replace the build with LDraw text (LDR or MPD). Returns its check. With expect, only while the build is still that text

expect.description: The build's text as last read (getModel): refused, nothing changed, once the build is no longer that text

charmiq.command.name: listDesigns
charmiq.command.description: The designs saved in the User's designs folder, each by name and uri

uri.description: The design's document: give it to loadDesign or defineComponentFromDesign

charmiq.command.name: loadDesign
charmiq.command.description: Replace the build with a saved design, by its uri from listDesigns (or its name). Returns its check

name.description: The design's name, when no uri is given

charmiq.command.name: saveDesign
charmiq.command.description: Save the build as a design in the User's designs folder (My Drive until they choose another). A name already there is refused unless replace is true

replace.description: Write over the design of that name
